findings.F1: The idea's effect is in the coin's longer scaled rise, not its 3-day rise. On every 7-day grid offset (7 non-overlapping grids, about 974 cases each, folds B and C), I regressed the 7-day unusual move on the prior return over the usual swing. The 14-day scaled return has a mean slope of 0.0151 with mean t 3.53, and its t is positive on all 7 offsets (1.62 to 4.56). The 3-day version has a mean t of 2.62, ranges from 0.88 to 4.72, and its first grid shows no clear slope in deciles. The 1-day version has a mean t of 1.39 and changes sign (from -3.11 to +5.21).
findings.F2: The 7-day scaled return is graded at its top. Averaged over the 7 grid offsets, its top quintile is followed by a 7-day unusual move of +2.45 % (std across offsets 0.54 %). The lower quintiles give -1.16 %, -0.20 %, -0.95 % and 0.00 %. On the offset-0 grid its top decile gives +3.77 % (t 1.94, 101 cases), against -2.58 % (t -1.88) for the bottom decile. That top-quintile move is about 13 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade.
findings.F3: The book earns where the 7-day scaled rise is high. Its mean bar return is +0.382 % with a mean allocation of 0.80 in the top tercile of the 7-day scaled return, +0.082 % (allocation 0.47) in the middle tercile, and -0.004 % (allocation 0.19) in the bottom one. Its Sharpe of 0.72 comes from the bars where the longer rise is large, not from the 3-day signal: the 3-day cases' mean unusual move is -0.30 %, t -0.67.
findings.F4: The continuation of the 7-day scaled rise is present in every trend, so it names no profile. The mean slope over offsets is 0.039 (t 2.50, about 87 cases per grid) in choppy markets, 0.020 (t 2.45, about 264) in falling markets and 0.017 (t 1.54, about 212) in rising markets. By year it is weak: mean t of 1.00, -0.02, 1.61 and 0.25 for 2018 to 2021.
findings.F5: A coin that falls unusually hard in one day rebounds the next day, and the rebound is graded. Over all bars, cases of one day taken together, the bottom decile of the 1-day return over the usual swing (median -1.57 swings) is followed by a next-day return of +1.14 % (t 2.57, 224 days). The second decile (median -0.84) is followed by +0.59 % (t 2.16, 363 days), and deciles 3 to 10 by between -0.24 % and +0.18 % (all |t| < 1). The rebound is several times the 0.19 % cost of a trade. It stands out moderately given the many angles I looked at.
findings.F6: Next-day returns by weekday are positive after Thursday and Friday bars: +0.61 % (t 1.93, 207 days) and +0.52 % (t 2.08, 206 days). They are positive in all four years for both days. It is a calendar effect with no graded situation, so I write no idea from it.

ideas.idea: A coin whose 14-day return is large against its usual daily swing (the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days) keeps rising over the next 7 days, and the larger that scaled 14-day rise, the larger the further gain.
ideas.consequence: A trader should hold a coin's longer rally that is unusual for that coin for the following week, rather than buying on a short 3-day burst.
ideas.name: scaled two-week rally continues

ideas.idea: A coin whose 7-day return is large against its usual daily swing (the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days) keeps rising over the next 7 days, and the larger that scaled 7-day rise, the larger the further gain.
ideas.consequence: A trader should buy, and hold for a week, a coin whose past week's rise is unusually large for it, sized by how unusual the rise is.
ideas.name: scaled weekly rally continues

ideas.idea: A coin whose 1-day return is a large fall against its usual daily swing (the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days) rises over the next day, and the larger that scaled one-day fall, the larger the rebound.
ideas.consequence: A trader should refuse to sell into, and may buy, a one-day drop that is unusually large for the coin, expecting part of it back the next day.
ideas.name: scaled one-day fall rebounds
